requirements.requirement: A host firewall is enabled on node1 and remains active with the intended policy after restart.
requirements.summary: Firewalld was active and enabled before the restart, with matching runtime and permanent public-zone policy. After the acknowledged restart and boot-ID change, firewalld was again active and enabled with the same policy and reject terminator.

requirements.requirement: Inbound SSH and TCP port 8080 are permitted.
requirements.summary: Runtime and permanent policy allow SSH and 8080/tcp. Isolated ingress tests directly observed an SSH banner and HTTP 200 on port 8080 both before and after restart.

Cockpit and DHCPv6-client allowances were removed, the active nftables input chain ended in an admin-prohibited rejection, and an isolated ingress test to a confirmed listening TCP/8081 service was rejected before and after restart while local control access succeeded.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Node1 has a persistent firewalld policy allowing SSH and TCP/8080 and rejecting unrelated inbound traffic. A complete restart transition showed a new boot identity, recovered services and policy, repeated traffic behavior, and clean final state.
limitations: Behavioral rejection testing sampled TCP/8081 over the isolated IPv4 ingress path rather than exhaustively probing every unrelated port, address family, and protocol; the active terminal reject rule provides supporting evidence for the broader policy.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The permanent firewall changes directly implemented the requested policy. Temporary namespaces, interfaces, listeners, transient services, and error files were bounded evidence prerequisites and were removed. The first cleanup left one test listener, but the corrective kill removed it; final checks and lifecycle observations show no test artifacts, extra listeners, failed services, or package damage. The restart was required by the provider-wide evidence protocol and was fully verified.
